sources.name: MLB StatsAPI active roster, Tampa Bay

flags.title: Eight fixtures could be proved, not the seventy-five the brief asks for
flags.detail: The brief asks for five priced matches per sport per day across fifteen sports, which is 75 books. This session confirmed eight fixtures end-to-end from official feeds: three MLB World Series games (2, 3 and 4) and five NHL games. Every other OLBG row is a listing without governing-body confirmation, so it is published as a watchlist row with no price. Nothing was imputed to reach a quota: the sports whose official routes failed carry unpriced listings rather than priced ones, and the two with nothing on offer carry no row at all.

flags.title: Golf: OLBG showed no event at all
flags.detail: The golf hub returned 'No tips found' at 16:41Z. Without an OLBG event there is no match to price, and no official PGA/DP World/LPGA field or tee sheet was retrieved either. Golf therefore has zero rows and zero picks in this release.

flags.title: Rugby League: OLBG lists outrights only
flags.detail: The rugby league hub showed State of Origin 2027, Super League 2027 and NRL 2027 winner markets, with no individual match. No match could be listed or priced.

flags.title: OLBG times are unlabelled and are not UTC
flags.detail: The same page mixes clock conventions: the MLB card read 'Today 20:00' for a 00:00 UTC start, while the WST card read 'Today 14:00' for a 13:00 UTC start. The greyhound hub is worse still: the row named 6:14 Monmore carried the clock 13:14, a seven-hour gap on a single line. This desk never uses an OLBG clock as a start time. Every start in the proved tables comes from the official feed; the OLBG label is shown beside it, verbatim, as a discovery artefact.

flags.title: Availability is only checkable for baseball, so hockey is capped at Medium
flags.detail: MLB StatsAPI publishes an active roster with a status per player, and both World Series clubs list 26 players all marked Active, so the three baseball rows carry a real availability statement. The NHL API roster endpoint returns biographical data only, with no injury or roster status field, and no club injury report was readable. The five hockey rows therefore have an empty availability field, and the published rule caps them at Medium for that reason alone. No press line or guess was used to fill the gap.

flags.title: Basketball: two-game samples cannot support a price
flags.detail: NBA standings on 24 October 2026 cover two games for most clubs. Shrunk win rates sit between .25 and .75, so almost every log5 output lands on a coin flip or an extreme. No NBA line was issued. The ten rows stay as listings for reference.

flags.title: Darts: the PDC schedule page was a cookie wall
flags.detail: Both pdc.tv URLs fetched rendered the consent dialogue instead of the match schedule. The five European Championship matches are therefore OLBG-only rows.

flags.title: Handball and volleyball: league sites did not render fixtures or tables
flags.detail: opel-hbl.de served a reCAPTCHA in place of the Spielplan and Tabelle, and legavolley.it returned navigation only. Handball and volleyball therefore have OLBG listings but no official confirmation and no prices.

flags.title: Greyhounds: no official racecard
flags.detail: No GBGB or track racecard was retrieved. Runner names on the greyhound rows come from OLBG's community tip cards and are shown as listing text only.

flags.title: Snooker final opponent undetermined at retrieval
flags.detail: WST lists the final as Kyren Wilson against the winner of match 62 (Mark Williams v Jak Jones). With one side unknown no two-way price can be originated, so the final is a watchlist row.

flags.title: Boston's fair price sits outside the brief's band
flags.detail: The Bruins' fair price is about -320, shorter than the -250 floor in the brief, so the selection is published as Medium even though the form case is the strongest on the slate. The price, not the argument, is what disqualifies it.

flags.title: The hockey samples are nine to twelve games old
flags.detail: Every NHL club has played between nine and twelve games, so a single result moves a win rate by roughly nine percentage points. The prices are published as snapshots with that stated, and no hockey pick is labelled High.

flags.title: The High tier holds one pick, because the brief's High test cannot be met more often
flags.detail: The brief asks a High pick to carry current form, recent history, match statistics and confirmed injuries, and to price between -250 and +10000. Only the World Series rows have all four: the rosters are checkable and both prices sit inside the band. Of the eight picks, one clears every condition, six are Medium and one is Low. Publishing six High labels would have meant ignoring the availability requirement.

flags.title: Each OLBG hub was read to its first screen only
flags.detail: Every sport hub truncates its card list and offers Load More Tips. The watchlist captures the rows rendered before that cut, plus the outright block where one appeared, so it is a sample of what OLBG advertised rather than a complete market list. Deeper pages were not consumed.

repo_audit.finding: The landing page's freshness chip says 'Snapshot 21 Oct 2026' while the body's data-snapshot attribute and data/current/site-manifest.json both say 2026-10-22T12:29:50Z. Two different snapshot dates are shown on one page.

The release summary quotes 108 captured listings and 42 statistical inputs. The manifest confirms 108 listings but records 32 source checks, not 42. The prose and the machine-readable manifest disagree.

219 fixture identifiers appear in more than one desk. mlb-849802, mlb-849804, mlb-849805 and nhl-2026020154/55 each occur in eight separate slates. The same event can therefore carry several different originated prices with nothing on the page saying which desk priced it or why they differ.
Row pdc-ec-03 uses the word 'verified' in published prediction prose, against the brief's instruction that the term stays internal.
The shared board is 733,636 bytes. A single file this large is slow to read and conflicts on nearly every rebase; it needs periodic archival by the integration session.
The publish job runs on main only, so a pull request cannot prove the deployed artifact. The PR gate builds and validates _site but never uploads it. This desk adds a local link gate to compensate.
